opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. As the role owning the Payroll system, admin is permitted for full-time employees. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E013 shows contractor with basic security training (not full-time as previously noted). Per policy, contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Requested: admin to Payroll. Security's record (looked up in own database) shows E013 is a contractor with basic security training, and explicitly notes the employee is not full-time. Per policy, contractors are never allowed admin; with only basic training, the maximum permitted level is read. Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum, the maximum (read) is granted.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time Payroll Specialist: admin allowed (role owns system). Requested admin → grant admin.
If contractor with basic training: max is read (no advanced training). Requested admin exceeds max → grant read.
